document_metadata.title: 1、EXT. MOVIE THEATRE - NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: An 18-year-old girl, Maureen, reluctantly waits in line with her boyfriend Phil for a free sneak preview of the horror movie 'STAB' at a small-town theater.

entities.description: A special advance screening of the movie 'Stab' is being held at a small-town movie theatre, drawing a large crowd of mostly college-aged attendees who have lined up around the block.

entities.description: Maureen proposes leaving the line to catch a different film starring Sandra Bullock, indicating a preference for a less frightening movie experience.

document_metadata.title: 10、INT. DORM ROOM - MORNING
document_metadata.summary: Sidney, disturbed by a TV interview linked to a past trauma, remains composed after a door prank, then leaves for a sorority rush with Hallie, showing resilience amid lingering unease.

entities.name: Sidney Prescott answers a prank phone call
entities.description: Sidney receives a mysterious phone call, identifies the caller as Cory Gillis using a phone tracing device, warns him about the legal consequences of prank calls, and hangs up.

entities.name: Sidney Prescott recognizes the caller's number
entities.description: Sidney uses a small device connected to the phone to trace the incoming call and identifies the caller by name and phone number.

entities.name: Hallie hands the phone to Sidney Prescott
entities.description: Hallie, Sidney's roommate, answers the ringing phone, speaks briefly with the caller, then passes the phone to Sidney.

entities.name: Sidney decides not to change her phone number
entities.description: After ending the prank call, Sidney declines Hallie's suggestion to change her number, believing the calls will stop after the movie's opening weekend.

entities.summary: A mature college student receives a prank call, identifies the caller, and is revealed as the killer's intended target, linking her to other victims and an alleged attack involving Cotton, with whom she shares a complex history.

entities.name: Sidney is ambushed by reporters outside her dorm
entities.description: Immediately after stepping outside her dorm, Sidney is surrounded by fifty news reporters who aggressively question her about murders she knows nothing about, shoving microphones and cameras in her face.

entities.name: Flashy reporter confronts Sidney with accusatory questions
entities.description: A flamboyant reporter blocks Sidney's path, wearing sunglasses and demanding to know if she killed people the previous night, intensifying Sidney's distress and anger.

entities.name: Gale Weathers punches the flashy reporter
entities.description: As the flashy reporter continues to harass Sidney, Gale Weathers emerges from the crowd and delivers a punch to the reporter's face, causing her to fall to the ground.

entities.name: Sidney and Gale share a brief moment of recognition
entities.description: After the punch, Sidney turns and sees Gale Weathers standing there; their eyes meet, conveying a quick, silent exchange of recognition and relief.

entities.name: Gale shields Sidney from the reporters
entities.description: Gale steps in front of Sidney, using her body to block the advancing reporters and creating a momentary barrier against the media onslaught.

entities.name: Gale instructs Sidney to escape while she holds off the crowd
entities.description: Gale tells Sidney to leave immediately and promises to find her later, allowing Sidney to flee the scene while Gale remains to face the reporters.

entities.name: Sidney flees around the side of the building
entities.description: Taking Gale's advice, Sidney runs around the side of her dorm building to escape the pursuing reporters, attempting to regain her composure.

entities.name: Reporters continue to pursue Sidney after her escape attempt
entities.description: Despite her attempt to get away, the reporters quickly follow Sidney around the building, maintaining pressure and refusing to let her go.

document_metadata.title: 15、INT. CLASSROOM - SAME
document_metadata.summary: Sidney watches a film debate where students critique sequels; Hallie likes JEDI's Ewoks, others dismiss sequels as profit-driven, Derek argues horror villains lose impact, then notices Sidney and approaches her.

entities.name: Sidney takes a seat at the back of the room unnoticed
entities.description: Sidney enters the room and sits at the back without drawing attention, observing the ongoing discussion among film students.

entities.name: Snotty Guy claims sequels are inherently inferior films
entities.description: A student referred to as Snotty Guy asserts that sequels are by definition inferior to original films, sparking a debate.

entities.name: Mickey argues that Aliens surpasses Alien
entities.description: Mickey counters the claim about sequel inferiority by asserting that 'Aliens' is far better than the original 'Alien'.

entities.name: Another Guy dismisses Mickey's claim as subjective
entities.description: An unnamed participant challenges Mickey's assertion by calling it a subjective opinion rather than an objective truth.

entities.name: Some Girl expresses preference for Ridley Scott's work
entities.description: A female participant in the discussion states her preference for director Ridley Scott, aligning with the Alien vs. Aliens debate.

entities.name: Hallie quotes 'Stay away from her - you bitch' from Aliens
entities.description: Hallie passionately defends Aliens by quoting a memorable line from the film, emphasizing its impact.

entities.name: Snotty Guy concedes one point but demands another example
entities.description: After Hallie's quote, Snotty Guy acknowledges the strength of that moment but insists on another example of a superior sequel.

entities.name: Mickey cites Terminator 2 as a superior sequel
entities.description: Mickey offers Terminator 2 as another example of a sequel surpassing its original, continuing the debate.

entities.name: Some Girl accuses Mickey of being biased toward Cameron
entities.description: A participant mocks Mickey by suggesting he is overly enthusiastic about James Cameron's films rather than being objective.

entities.name: Snotty Guy argues Terminator 1 is historically significant
entities.description: Snotty Guy counters the praise for T2 by asserting the historical importance and superiority of the original Terminator.

entities.name: Someone shouts 'You Sarah Connor?' during the debate
entities.description: An unidentified person interrupts the discussion with a humorous shout referencing a line from the Terminator films.

entities.name: Artsy Teacher proposes The Godfather Part II as a superior sequel
entities.description: The teacher in the room intervenes by citing The Godfather Part II as an example of a sequel that is widely respected.

entities.name: The room falls into reverent silence over The Godfather Part II
entities.description: Upon mention of The Godfather Part II, all students stop arguing and show collective respect, indicating consensus on its greatness.

entities.name: Snotty Guy acknowledges The Godfather Part II as the exception
entities.description: Snotty Guy concedes that The Godfather Part II is a rare case of a superior sequel but challenges others to name another.

entities.name: Derek enters the debate citing Empire Strikes Back as superior
entities.description: A new participant, Derek, joins the conversation by arguing that The Empire Strikes Back improves upon the original Star Wars film.

entities.name: Sidney becomes fixated on Derek from the back of the room
entities.description: As Derek speaks, Sidney, who has been quietly observing, becomes intensely focused on him, indicating a personal reaction.

entities.summary: A confident film student and TKE member involved with Hallie, he supports her at rehearsals and events, participates in a fundraiser, coaches during an eating contest, and balances band commitments with his relationship, showing concern for friends like Derek.

entities.name: Hallie expresses liking for Jedi featuring Ewoks
entities.description: Hallie states her enjoyment of the film Jedi, specifically mentioning the furry Ewoks, which prompts a negative reaction from others in the room.

entities.name: Film students react negatively to Hallie's Ewok comment
entities.description: Multiple students boo and derisively comment 'Ewoks blow' in response to Hallie's positive remark about the Ewoks in Jedi.

entities.name: Mickey mocks Lucas with a Romper Room stage comparison
entities.description: Mickey ridicules George Lucas by comparing his filmmaking to a childish Romper Room stage, implying a lack of artistic seriousness.

entities.name: Hallie suggests Friday the 13th Part 20 as a film example
entities.description: Hallie proposes 'Friday the 13th, Part 20' as a title, likely in jest or to illustrate the absurdity of endless sequels within the horror genre.

entities.name: Snotty Guy claims horror genre was destroyed by sequels
entities.description: Snotty Guy asserts that the horror genre has been ruined due to the proliferation of sequels, citing it as a prime example of sequel degradation.

entities.name: Artsy Teacher challenges Snotty Guy to explain his reasoning
entities.description: The Artsy Teacher questions Snotty Guy's claim about horror sequels, prompting him to elaborate on why he believes sequels are detrimental.

entities.name: Snotty Guy attributes sequel decline to profit over quality
entities.description: Snotty Guy argues that sequels prioritize financial gain over artistic quality, leading to a decline in film integrity and creativity.

entities.name: Derek analyzes horror sequel weakness through villain dilution
entities.description: Derek explains that horror sequels fail because their villains, like Freddy and Jason, lose their fear factor after repeated appearances across multiple sequels.

entities.name: Artsy Teacher poses a creative challenge about sequel improvement
entities.description: The Artsy Teacher asks the class how they would improve a sequel if they were making one, prompting reflective silence among the students.

entities.name: Derek notices Sidney and approaches her after turning around
entities.description: Derek turns and sees Sidney sitting in the back of the room, who waves at him; he then gets up and walks toward her, excusing himself from the group.

entities.name: Snotty Guy declares he has proven his point about sequels
entities.description: After the discussion, Snotty Guy asserts that his argument against sequels has been validated and concludes that 'sequels suck'.

document_metadata.summary: Sidney realizes Gale set her up, confronts her, and storms off; Cotton leaves, regretting his involvement. Randy filmed it but is unhappy. Gale dismisses remorse, prioritizing the story.

entities.description: Lois takes two rolls of toilet paper from her book bag and hands them out to the pledges as part of a fundraising initiative.

entities.name: Murphy announces the toilet paper fundraiser with a five-dollar quota
entities.description: Murphy explains to the pledges that they are expected to sell individual squares of toilet paper for five dollars each to support the TKE kegger.

entities.name: Sidney accepts her share of toilet paper despite objections
entities.description: Sidney insists on participating in the fundraiser, takes her roll of toilet paper, and rejects Derek's suggestion that she shouldn't have to, showing her determination to be treated equally.

entities.description: Before departing with Hallie, Sidney gives him a reassuring look to indicate she is okay with the situation, strengthening their emotional connection.

entities.description: Derek questions how Mickey tolerates the fraternity culture, calling it 'Greek shit' and showing his disapproval of the ongoing fundraiser.

entities.name: Mickey justifies his involvement in the fundraiser through loyalty to Hallie
entities.description: Mickey responds to Derek by stating that he supports the event because Hallie is involved, and his commitment stems from his feelings for her.

entities.name: Dewey confronts Gale about her book's portrayal of him
entities.description: Dewey rebukes Gale for depicting him negatively in her book, citing specific passages that insult his intelligence and character, expressing deep personal offense.

entities.name: Gale apologizes to Dewey for the hurtful descriptions in her book
entities.description: Gale attempts to make amends by sincerely apologizing to Dewey, acknowledging the pain her writing caused and expressing regret.

entities.name: Dewey rejects Gale's apology and accuses her of being heartless
entities.description: Dewey responds to Gale's apology by calling her a fame-seeking liar and a mediocre writer with emotional coldness, refusing to accept her remorse.

entities.name: Dewey claims his perceived incompetence is a strategic advantage
entities.description: Dewey challenges Gale's assumptions by suggesting that his 'dim-witted' image is a deliberate tactic to manipulate expectations and improve his situational effectiveness.

entities.name: Dewey ends the confrontation and limps away from Gale
entities.description: After delivering a final sarcastic remark about having 'oozing' to do, Dewey turns and walks away, leaving Gale visibly devastated by the encounter.

entities.description: Sidney moves to the shed attached to the garage, chooses a shovel from a row of garden tools, and takes it back toward Mickey.

entities.name: Sidney strikes the lock with a shovel
entities.description: Sidney lifts the shovel and brings it down on the lock binding Mickey, causing it to bend but remain intact.

entities.name: Sidney cracks the lock with a powerful shovel strike
entities.description: Sidney raises the shovel high and strikes the lock with great force, cracking it and loosening its hold, though it does not fully break.

entities.name: Ghost Masked Figure descends from a tree behind Sidney
entities.description: While Sidney prepares to strike the lock again, the Ghost Masked Figure silently slides down from a tree branch and takes a stance behind her unnoticed.

entities.name: Mickey warns Sidney of imminent danger
entities.description: Mickey sees the Ghost Masked Figure behind Sidney and shouts a warning just as the Killer is about to strike.

entities.name: Sidney swings shovel at Ghost Masked Figure
entities.description: Sidney turns and instinctively swings the shovel at the Ghost Masked Figure, striking him in the mid-section and sending him flying.

entities.description: Chained to a tree, Mickey pulls, twists, and squirms violently in an attempt to break free from the bike chain binding him.

entities.name: Sidney distracts Ghost Masked Figure to protect Mickey
entities.description: Seeing the Ghost advance on Mickey, Sidney calls out and draws the attacker's attention, then runs to lead him away.

entities.name: Sidney collides with Ghost Masked Figure during pursuit
entities.description: While fleeing across the yard to distract the killer, Sidney sprints around the tree and runs directly into the Ghost Masked Figure who has intercepted her path.

entities.summary: A young woman faces intense media scrutiny and social pressure after a series of murders linked to a film; she quietly observes a class, fixates on Derek, and navigates personal relationships while avoiding public attention.

entities.summary: A confident film student and TKE member involved with Hallie, he supports her at rehearsals and events, participates in a fundraiser, coaches during an eating contest, and balances band commitments with his relationship, showing concern for friends like Derek.

document_metadata.title: 71、INT. THEATRE SAME
document_metadata.summary: Sidney confronts Derek and Hallie, who reveal their year-long plot to terrorize her, inspired by killer couples; Derek stops her from freeing Cotton, asserting control.

entities.name: Sidney unlocks and enters the theatre through a side house door
entities.description: Sidney enters the old, large theatre by pulling open a side door, releasing its emergency lock, and proceeds down the aisle toward the orchestra section.

entities.name: Sidney calls out into the dark theatre
entities.description: Standing in the orchestra area, Sidney calls out 'Hello?' into the dark and seemingly empty theatre, which contains only the furniture from the DEATHTRAP set.

entities.name: Loud bump noise occurs in the stage wings
entities.description: A sudden bumping sound comes from one of the stage wings, prompting Sidney to react and investigate further.

entities.name: Sidney moves to stage center to investigate
entities.description: Sidney proceeds from the orchestra pit across a small bridge and onto the stage, moving to center stage and peering into both wings in the darkness.

entities.name: Liquid drips onto Sidney from above
entities.description: A substance drips from the ceiling onto Sidney's face, which she wipes off, only to discover it is crimson in color.

entities.name: Spotlight suddenly illuminates Sidney on stage
entities.description: A spotlight abruptly turns on from the back of the theatre, shining directly on Sidney at center stage, startling her.

entities.name: Sidney discovers blood on her hand
entities.description: After the spotlight activates, Sidney looks at her hand and sees it covered in blood, realizing the dripping substance was not water.

entities.name: Set wall plummets from above toward Sidney
entities.description: Ropes and pulleys activate with a clanking noise, causing a large set wall to crash down from the flies toward Sidney, who narrowly escapes.

entities.name: Sidney narrowly avoids being crushed by falling set wall
entities.description: Sidney leaps aside just in time as a heavy set wall crashes down onto the stage, avoiding serious injury but falling to the floor in shock.

entities.name: Dewey's corpse revealed on fallen set wall
entities.description: The set wall that falls into place displays Dewey's dead body, pinned and crucified against it, arms outstretched, covered in blood.

entities.name: Sidney reacts in horror to Dewey's body
entities.description: Sidney freezes in shock and terror upon seeing Dewey's gruesome corpse, overwhelmed by the sight and breaking into tears.

entities.name: Sidney attempts to flee toward the wings
entities.description: Traumatized by the discovery of Dewey's body, Sidney backs away and runs toward the stage wings in an attempt to escape.

entities.name: Second set wall seals off the backstage area
entities.description: As Sidney runs toward the wings, a second set wall swings in from above, blocking access to the backstage and trapping her on stage.

entities.name: Hallie's corpse revealed hanging in the wings
entities.description: After the second wall seals the stage, Hallie's lifeless body is revealed, strung up and hanging in the now-visible wing area.

entities.name: Sidney screams and runs across the stage
entities.description: Upon seeing Hallie's dead body, Sidney lets out a scream and sprints toward the opposite side of the stage in panic.

entities.name: Third set wall completes the DEATHTRAP set
entities.description: A third wall flies in and locks into place, forming the full three-walled configuration of the DEATHTRAP stage set.

entities.name: Joel's corpse revealed attached to the third set wall
entities.description: Joel's dead body is discovered attached to the third set wall as it locks into place, bloodied and lifeless, completing the macabre scene.

entities.name: theatre
entities.description: A large, old building with a stage, balcony, and orchestra section where the events unfold.

entities.name: side house door
entities.description: An entrance to the theatre located at the side, used by Sidney to enter the building.

entities.description: The pathway between rows of plush chairs leading from the entrance toward the orchestra section of the theatre.

entities.description: The main floor area of the theatre seating, located in front of the stage.

entities.name: stage wings
entities.description: The off-stage areas to the left and right of the proscenium stage where noises and bodies are discovered.

entities.description: A small walkway extending from the front of the stage across the orchestra pit.

entities.summary: A young woman faces intense media scrutiny and social pressure after a series of murders linked to a film; she quietly observes a class, fixates on Derek, and navigates personal relationships while avoiding public attention.

entities.name: Dewey Riley
entities.description: A man found dead, crucified on a falling set wall in the theatre, part of a macabre stage setup.
entities.summary: Multiple individuals, including a security officer, deputy, independent investigator, and silent observer, interact with key characters amid an ongoing murder investigation, revealing tensions, strategic behaviors, and new clues about the killer's target.

entities.name: Hallie
entities.description: A woman found hanging lifeless in the stage wings after Sidney triggers a trap in the theatre.
entities.summary: A group of students and friends, including Sidney's roommate, film enthusiasts, and sorority and fraternity members, interact during a monitored event, showing varied reactions to Sidney and each other.

entities.name: Joel
entities.description: A man found dead, attached to the third set wall that completes the DEATHTRAP stage set.
entities.summary: A concerned, intelligent student in his twenties knows Sidney's history, contributes insights on Randy Meeks and serial killers, checks outside, plans to meet after class, and is connected to Derek; another man arrives with police, vouched by Sidney, while a man is found dead on the DEATHTRAP set.

entities.description: A locking mechanism on the side house door that Sidney releases upon entry to the theatre.

entities.description: A light fixture activated from the back of the house that suddenly illuminates Sidney on stage.

entities.description: A large stage prop that plummets from above, used as part of a deadly trap in the theatre.

entities.name: blood
entities.description: A substance dripping from above onto Sidney, later revealed to come from the corpses on the set walls.

entities.name: Sidney hears clapping from a figure in the theatre aisle
entities.description: Sidney hears a single pair of hands clapping from somewhere in the house and turns to see a figure moving down the aisle, though she cannot identify who it is.

entities.name: Sidney attempts to escape through the set door near Dewey's body
entities.description: Sidney runs toward the set door located up center near Dewey's corpse, attempting to use it as an escape route.

entities.name: Sidney encounters Cotton Weary bound in the doorway
entities.description: Sidney opens the set door to find Cotton Weary standing in the doorway, his arms and legs bound with electric tape, appearing scared and pleading for help.

entities.name: Sidney screams upon seeing Cotton Weary in distress
entities.description: Startled and frightened, Sidney screams when she suddenly sees Cotton Weary bound and immobilized in the doorway.

entities.name: Derek reveals himself as the figure filming Sidney
entities.description: The figure walking across the little bridge over the orchestra pit pulls away a video camera to reveal himself as Derek, who smiles at Sidney while continuing to film her.

entities.name: Derek taunts Sidney with a reference to a familiar narrative
entities.description: From behind the camera, Derek speaks to Sidney, saying 'You've seen this movie before, haven't you?' in a mocking tone, implying a sense of predestined repetition.

entities.name: Derek instructs Sidney to smile for the camera
entities.description: Derek directly addresses Sidney, telling her to 'smile for the camera' while filming her reaction, further asserting control over the situation.

entities.name: Cotton pleads with Sidney to untie him
entities.description: While bound on the floor, Cotton looks up at Sidney with desperate eyes and urges her to free him, warning that Derek will kill them both.

entities.name: Sidney hesitates to untie Cotton due to distrust
entities.description: Sidney begins to lean down to untie Cotton but stops, expressing fear and uncertainty about whether helping him is safe or part of a trap.

entities.name: Sidney refuses to untie Cotton under Derek's pressure
entities.description: When Derek challenges her, Sidney firmly says 'No,' recognizing the situation as a setup and refusing to comply with his apparent expectations.

entities.name: Derek resumes filming Sidney with mocking commentary
entities.description: Derek starts recording Sidney again while commenting on her psychological state, suggesting she is struggling with trust issues.

entities.name: Sidney retreats toward Hallie's hanging body
entities.description: Feeling threatened and uncertain whom to trust, Sidney edges away from both Cotton and Derek, moving back toward the wall where Hallie's corpse is hanging.

entities.name: Debbie Salt reveals her motive for the killing spree
